digest.en: Houthis claim strikes on Riyadh airport while Rubio tours Central Asia to counter Russian and Chinese influence. Sudan’s war expands through drone attacks and famine as the Kremlin avoids formal mobilization.
digest.hi: मेरठ में दो दिन में चार दोषियों को फांसी दी गई, जिससे पश्चिमी यूपी की पांच महिलाओं की सज़ाएँ भी सुनाई गईं। इसी घंटे ट्रंप प्रशासन महिलाओं के पदों से हटाने की प्रक्रिया तेज कर रहा है।

articles.title: Yemen’s Houthis say struck Riyadh airport, other Saudi sites
articles.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Riyadh airport and other Saudi locations. The United Nations reports the conflict has displaced over 184,000 people. This makes Yemen the region's most active front. The fighting continues to deepen the wider regional crisis. The fighting in Yemen has become the most active front in the West Asia war in recent weeks, displacing more than 1,84,000 people, the United Nations says, and deepening the conflict that has engulfed the wider region.

articles.title: Reopening Brexit debate a ‘terrible idea’: Conservative leader Badenoch
articles.summary: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch called reopening the Brexit debate a terrible idea. She argued the process wasted significant time on internal and EU arguments. Badenoch emphasized the need to avoid repeating that circular political process. “Can you imagine having to go through that again?

articles.title: Brazilian Amazon deforestation falls to lowest on record as pivotal vote looms
articles.summary: Brazilian Amazon deforestation hit its lowest recorded level since 1988, according to new government data. This decline marks a significant policy win for President Lula ahead of the 25 October presidential run-off. The sustainability of this progress remains uncertain as voters choose between candidates with diverging environmental stances. The election outcome will directly determine whether these conservation gains hold or reverse.

articles.title: No 10 leaves option open to impose Chinese EV tariffs if UK joins EU scheme
articles.summary: Downing Street confirmed the UK may impose tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles if it joins the EU's Made in Europe package. Beijing warned the measure would be discriminatory. France dropped its opposition to British participation in the scheme. The decision remains pending final negotiations. Beijing warns against ‘discriminatory’ step after France drops opposition to British role in Made in Europe packageNo 10 has left the door open to imposing tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles as part of the Made in Europe package, prompting a warning from Beijing that such a move would be “discriminatory”. articles.title: Russia Still Needs More Soldiers. The Kremlin Is Still Desperate To Avoid Mobilization
articles.summary: Russia continues quiet mobilization to replace losses in Ukraine. The Kremlin avoided a formal national draft order after recent elections. Coercive recruiting tactics persist across the country. Military forces remain depleted despite ongoing combat operations. Many Russians feared the Kremlin would order a new mobilization after last month’s elections: to replenish decimated forces fighting in Ukraine. That hasn’t happened. But creative and coercive recruiting tactics – called “quiet” or “creeping” mobilization by some – continue nationwide.

articles.title: Sudan’s war spreads as drones and hunger take a deadly toll
articles.summary: Drone strikes are killing civilians across El Obeid and Blue Nile. Famine risk is spreading through Darfur and Kordofan. The Security Council met to address the world's largest hunger and displacement crisis. Ambassadors pressed for a ceasefire, safe aid access, and a halt to weapons flows. As drone strikes kill civilians from El Obeid to Blue Nile and famine risk spreads across Darfur and Kordofan, the Security Council meets on Sudan – the world’s largest hunger and displacement crisis.

articles.title: Russia's Shadow War On NATO Is 'Bound To Intensify'
articles.summary: Russia's shadow war against NATO involves drone incursions, sabotage, and assassination attempts. Christopher Walker of the Center for European Policy Analysis says the campaign is approaching a crucial point. The strategy has largely backfired by drawing a resolute response. He predicts the conflict will continue to intensify. Russia's shadow campaign of drone incursions, sabotage, and assassination attempts in NATO countries has largely backfired by drawing a resolute response but is approaching a "crucial point," Christopher Walker, vice president of the Center for European Policy Analysis, tells RFE/RL.

articles.title: Hot US inflation singes Asia as higher-for-longer Fed rates loom
articles.summary: September US inflation hit 3.7% year-on-year, exceeding forecasts. The data suggests the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates higher for longer. Asian markets face renewed pressure on currencies, capital flows, and economic growth from this sustained monetary tightening. TOKYO. An unwelcome blast of US inflation is blowing across Asia’s markets. September’s hotter-than-expected price data revived concerns that the Federal Reserve will keep rates higher for longer, threatening fresh pressure on currencies, capital flows and economic growth across the region.

articles.title: Zelenskyy Says US Diesel Deal Will Put Money 'Straight Into Putin's Pocket'
articles.summary: Nine US senators requested an investigation into satellite system disruptions affecting Ukraine’s military. The bipartisan group acted as European officials rallied around Kyiv. This occurred after President Trump again criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during the EU summit. A bipartisan group of nine US senators has called for an investigation into disruptions to satellite systems supporting Ukraine's military as European officials rallied around Kyiv after President Donald Trump again attacked his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

articles.title: Rubio Heads To Central Asia As US Seeks Bigger Role In Region Dominated By Russia, China
articles.summary: Marco Rubio travels to Uzbekistan to meet with five Central Asian nations. The Trump administration aims to strengthen commercial ties and expand US strategic presence. The region has historically been dominated by Russian and Chinese influence. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio heads to Uzbekistan this weekend for talks with five Central Asian countries as the Trump administration seeks to strengthen commercial ties and expand Washington's strategic presence in the region.

articles.title: What do North Korea’s sub missile tests really prove?
articles.summary: North Korea test-fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles into the Sea of Japan. This marks the country's first public underwater launch of such weapons. The tests demonstrate a push to build a survivable, sea-based nuclear deterrent. However, significant engineering hurdles and platform limitations still constrain its naval capabilities. The exercises highlight a shift toward diversifying its delivery systems beyond land-based missiles.

articles.title: Attacking Trump, Zelensky showed lack of judgment
articles.summary: Volodymyr Zelensky criticized Donald Trump after Ukraine struck two Russian oil refineries. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Aleksandr Novak confirmed the attacks on the facilities. Zelensky had previously thwarted a US request to avoid targeting Russian energy infrastructure. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky’s harsh words about US President Donald Trump were an emotional response after Zelensky deliberately thwarted Trump’s request that Ukraine not strike Russian refineries.

articles.title: Milei adviser claims UK being ‘colonised by Islam’ as Falklands row grows
articles.summary: Santiago Caputo, adviser to Argentine President Milei, claimed the UK is being colonized by Islam. He cited the election of MP Sagal Abdi-Wali as evidence. The post supports Argentina's push for sovereignty over the Falkland Islands. Santiago Caputo cites election of Sagal Abdi-Wali as MP and calls UK a threat to the west in post shared by Argentina’s presidentThe chief adviser to Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, has cited the election of Sagal Abdi-Wali to the UK parliament as evidence of the Islamisation of Britain and further reason for Argentina to take sovereignty over the Falkland Islands. In a post on social media, S.

articles.title: Tech market sell-off deepens amid fears over US inflation and AI debt
articles.summary: Global tech markets suffered a deep sell-off driven by inflation fears and AI sector debt. Shares in Samsung and SoftBank plunged as traders worried about potential interest rate hikes. The decline reflects growing anxiety over the heavy borrowing underpinning current artificial intelligence infrastructure. Chip makers and tech investors such as Samsung and SoftBank plunge as potential interest rate hikes spook marketsBusiness news – live updatesLarry Elliott: the global economy is muddling through.

articles.title: Afghanistan faces record hunger levels amid rampant rights violations
articles.summary: Afghanistan faces record hunger levels with 15.9 million people facing acute food insecurity. A global hunger monitor report released Thursday confirmed these are the highest levels ever recorded. Conditions are expected to worsen significantly in the coming months due to ongoing rights violations. Acute malnutrition and hunger in Afghanistan have reached the highest levels ever recorded, with 15.9 million people facing acute food insecurity and conditions set to worsen in the coming months, according to a global hunger monitor report released on Thursday.

articles.title: The world is waging a ‘war on nature’ as progress on biodiversity targets lags
articles.summary: The UN warns fewer than half of national biodiversity targets are on track. This report arrives days before the COP17 conference in Yerevan, Armenia. The assessment highlights a significant gap in global efforts to protect plants, animals, and ecosystems from further degradation. Fewer than half of the national targets set to protect the world’s plants, animals and ecosystems are on track, the UN warns in a new report, days before countries gather in Yerevan, Armenia, for the COP17 biodiversity conference.

articles.title: AI, green energy and economic transitions risk leaving vulnerable communities behind, UN warns
articles.summary: A new UN report warns rapid transitions in AI, green energy, and demographics risk deepening inequalities. These shifts are reshaping economies worldwide while creating new opportunities. Vulnerable communities face the greatest threat of being left behind by these structural changes. Rapid transformations – from artificial intelligence and digital technologies to renewable energy and demographic shifts – are reshaping economies worldwide, creating new opportunities but also threatening to deepen socio-economic inequalities, a new UN report warned on Thursday.

articles.title: WHO urges faster action to end lead exposure which kills 3.5 million annually
articles.summary: The World Health Organization urged nations to accelerate lead exposure prevention efforts. The toxic metal causes over 3.5 million deaths annually. It also affects hundreds of millions of children worldwide. The agency called for faster action to address this persistent public health crisis. Countries must accelerate efforts to prevent lead exposure, which is estimated to cause more than 3.5 million deaths globally each year and affects hundreds of millions of children, the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Thursday.

articles.title: Could your brain data be used against you? UN calls for limits on neurotechnology
articles.summary: A new UN report warns neurotechnology outpaces human rights laws. Brain data from gaming or wellness devices could become court evidence. The organization called for limits on these technologies. Current legal frameworks fail to protect individuals from misuse. Brain signals recorded by a gaming headset or a wellness gadget could one day be used as evidence against you in court, according to a new UN report which warns that neurotechnology is outpacing the laws meant to protect human rights.

articles.title: Zelenskyy Vows Refinery Strikes, Expresses Anger At US Intel Disruption
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces struck an oil refinery in Russia's Ryazan region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the resumption of attacks on Russian energy facilities. He also expressed anger over a dangerous disruption of US satellite intelligence that hindered Ukrainian operations. Ukrainian forces have struck an oil refinery in Russia's Ryazan region, Russian officials said, hours after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine would resume attacks on Russian energy facilities and voiced anger over a "dangerous" disruption of satellite intelligence from the United States.

articles.title: LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested
articles.summary: Senegal authorities detained more than 320 LGBTQ+ individuals since February after the government tightened its law criminalising homosexuality. The arrests triggered forced HIV testing and limited access to legal representation, according to a Human Rights Watch report. The crackdown signals a broader clamp At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reportsMass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a new report. More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, accor.

articles.title: Indonesia fights fire with dry ice as toxic haze spreads across region
articles.summary: Indonesia is testing dry ice dispersal in South Sumatra. The government deployed planes to combat toxic haze. This follows failed cloud seeding attempts. Regional neighbors remain angry over the smoke. Having tried cloud seeding and water bombing, one pilot project will see dry ice dispersed by plane across the province of South SumatraAs fires ravage Indonesia, emitting a toxic smoke that has drawn the ire of regional neighbours, the government is testing an unusual new approach to tackle the haze: dry ice. Having tried cloud seeding, water bombing and sending in army personnel to fight the fire.

articles.title: Girls In Hijabs Turned Away From Azerbaijani Schools Amid Protests Over Dress Code
articles.summary: Azerbaijani parents and students protested after schools turned away girls wearing hijabs. The action followed a new ban on clothing deemed incompatible with secular education. The dispute has sparked public backlash over the dress code enforcement in public schools. A new dress-code dispute in Azerbaijan’s public schools has sparked protests by parents and students after reports that girls wearing hijabs, or Islamic headscarf, were turned away from classes.

articles.title: Ukraine Tests AI-Powered Drones As Debate Grows Over Autonomous Weapons
articles.summary: Ukraine is deploying artificial intelligence in drones to track and engage targets. Military officials confirm humans retain control over lethal decisions. Developers caution that fully autonomous weapons systems are approaching operational reality on the battlefield. Ukraine is increasingly using artificial intelligence in drones and other battlefield systems to track, identify, and attack targets. Military officials say humans still remain in control of lethal decisions, but developers warn that fully autonomous weapons are moving closer to reality.

articles.title: Guinea-Bissau denies it has approved controversial vaccine trial in newborns
articles.summary: Guinea-Bissau's health minister stated the government did not authorize a Danish-led hepatitis B trial in newborns. The study, backed by the US government and private partners, would not test vaccine safety or effectiveness. The ministry denied approval for the controversial research. Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK JrGuinea-Bissau has not approved the controversial hepatitis B study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday. articles.summary: नासा के सैटेलाइट डेटा के अनुसार प्रशांत महासागर में जलस्तर 40 सेंटीमीटर तक बढ़ गया है। नोआ का अनुमान है कि यह 1950 के बाद का सबसे ताकतवर अल नीनो होगा। समंदर का रंग हरे से नीला हो गया है। नासा के सैटेलाइट्स प्रशांत महासागर में बन रहे ऐतिहासिक अल नीनो को ट्रैक कर रहे हैं. नोआ के अनुसार 83 प्रतिशत संभावना है कि यह 1950 के बाद का सबसे ताकतवर अल नीनो होगा.

articles.title: बालेन शाह के दौरे से पहले भारत ने खेला कूटनीतिक कार्ड, सीनियर डिप्लोमैट सुधाकर दलेला को राजदूत बना
articles.summary: भारत ने नेपाल में सुधाकर दलेला को अगला राजदूत नियुक्त किया है। यह नियुक्ति प्रधानमंत्री बालेन शाह के अगले महीने होने वाले भारत दौरे से ठीक पहले हुई। पहली बार सेक्रेटरी रैंक के अधिकारी को काठमांडू भेजा गया है। विदेश मंत्रालय के सचिव सुधाकर दलेला को नेपाल में भारत का अगला राजदूत नियुक्त किया गया है. दलेला वरिष्ठ राजनयिक नवीन श्रीवास्तव की जगह लेंगे जिनका तीन साल का कार्यकाल पूरा हो चुका है.

articles.title: हूती हमलों की आग में ‘मक्का समझौता’: सऊदी की मदद के लिए पाकिस्तान का सधा हुआ डिप्लोमेटिक दांव
articles.summary: यमन के हूती विद्रोहियों के सऊदी अरब पर मिसाइल और ड्रोन हमलों ने मक्का संयुक्त रक्षा समझौते को परीक्षा में डाल दिया है। इस त्रिपक्षीय समझौते के तहत सऊदी, पाकिस्तान और तुर्किए में से किसी एक पर हमला तीनों पर हमला माना जाएगा। सऊदी अरब पर यमन के हूती विद्रोहियों के भीषण मिसाइल और ड्रोन हमलों ने अगस्त 2026 में हुए ऐतिहासिक ‘मक्का संयुक्त रक्षा समझौते’ (Mecca Joint Defence Agreement) को बड़ी परीक्षा में डाल दिया है।
